mainTopic: Which items stay on the מזבח once they go up, and the פסוקים each תנא uses to learn it
overview: The גמרא begins with the משנה's rule that the מזבח keeps only items 'suited to it.' רב פפא says this leaves out a קמיצה that was never placed in a כלי שרת, because it is still missing an action on itself. Next, the גמרא works through how רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל each read the words 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.' Along the way it learns the rules about putting back pieces that fell off the fire, and why burnt קטורת is not put back. It also explains why רבי יהושע needs two 'מזבח' פסוקים and רבן גמליאל does not. Then a ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's source: only items that come for their own sake stay up, so נסכים come down. Another ברייתא has רבי יוסי הגלילי learning the rule from 'כבשים' and רבי עקיבא learning it from 'עולה.' They differ over a disqualified bird עולה, and between them they leave out a מנחה. רב פפא shows that this puts them against the תנאים of our משנה on disqualified קמצים. ריש לקיש then begins a summary, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'suited to it' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's words 'suited to it' and asks which item they come to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Things suited to the מזבח, yes, they stay on it. Things not suited to it, no. What is this coming to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by reading the משנה's phrase 'רָאוּי לוֹ' closely. It asks what kind of item this phrase is meant to rule out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says only suitable items stay on the מזבח, then some item must not count as suitable. The גמרא wants to know which item that is. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Suited to it, meaning fit for the מזבח

phrases.english: Gemara:
Things suited to it [the altar], yes,
things not suited to it, no;
to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item is ruled out by the משנה's words 'suited to it'?

steps.title: A handful of flour not yet placed in a holy vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase excludes a קמיצה that was never put into a כלי שרת. Such a קמיצה comes down even if it went up on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It excludes handfuls of flour that were not made holy in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. A handful of flour from a מנחה that went up on the מזבח before it was placed in a כלי שרת is not 'suited,' so it comes down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קמיצה becomes fit for the מזבח only after it is placed in a כלי שרת. Without that step it never became fit. So it falls outside 'רָאוּי לוֹ' and does not stay on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Handfuls of flour taken from a מִנְחָה to be burned
Made holy by being placed in a holy vessel (כְּלִי שָׁרֵת)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
to exclude handfuls [of flour]
that were not sanctified in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קמיצה not yet placed in a כלי שרת is not 'suited,' so it comes down from the מזבח.

steps.title: רבינא challenges from עולא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why the קמיצה is different from עולא's case. In that case, אימורים offered before the blood was sprinkled stay on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged: How is this different from עולא's ruling? עולא said: if someone put the אימורים of קדשים קלים on the מזבח before the blood was sprinkled, they do not come down. They have become the 'bread of the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב פפא. In עולא's case, the parts were also not yet ready for the מזבח, yet they stay up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the blood is sprinkled, the אימורים are not yet fit to be burned. Still, עולא says they stay on the מזבח. So why should the unready קמיצה come down?

keyTerms.meaning: Parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
The 'bread' of the מזבח, meaning it now belongs to the מזבח

phrases.english: Ravina objected to it:
what is different from [the ruling] of Ulla?
For Ulla said:
sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity
that one offered up before the sprinkling of their blood –
shall not descend,
they have become the bread of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא: מַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that an unready קמיצה comes down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא rules that unready אימורים stay up, so unreadiness alone should not make the קמיצה come down.

steps.title: Missing an action on itself versus waiting for a separate action
steps.stepSummary: The אימורים are not missing any action on themselves; only the blood still needs to be sprinkled. The קמיצה is missing an action on itself: being placed in the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: These (the אימורים) are not missing an action on their own body. These (the קמיצה) are missing an action on their own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אימורים themselves are complete; they are only waiting for something else to happen, the sprinkling of the blood. The קמיצה itself still needs to be placed in a כלי שרת, so it never became fit. That is why the אימורים stay up and the קמיצה comes down.

keyTerms.meaning: On their own body, to the item itself

steps.whatToRemember: An item that is missing an action on itself, like a קמיצה not yet in a כלי שרת, is not 'suited' and comes down. An item waiting only for a separate action, like אימורים waiting for the blood, stays up.

phrases.english: Those do not lack an action on themselves,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means עולא's אימורים; they are only waiting for the blood to be sprinkled.

phrases.english: these lack an action on themselves.
phrases.notes: 'These' means רב פפא's handfuls, which still need to be put in the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both items are not yet ready, so they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Missing an action on the item itself makes it unsuited; waiting for an outside action does not.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבן גמליאל learn from 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's view, which is based on the פסוק 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה.' It asks: doesn't רבן גמליאל also have this פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Anything suited to the fire, etc. And as for רבן גמליאל too, isn't it written 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי יהושע's view. It challenges רבן גמליאל: the פסוק רבי יהושע uses is in the תורה for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע learns from 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה' that only things fit for the fire stay up. רבן גמליאל includes everything fit for the מזבח, even things not burned. So how does he deal with this פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
anything suited to the fires, etc.
And Rabban Gamliel too –
isn't it written: "Burnt offering on the pyre"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to limit the rule to things fit for the fire, which goes against רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches returning pieces that fell off
steps.stepSummary: According to רבן גמליאל, 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה' teaches that pieces that jumped off the fire must be put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to teach that pieces that jumped off the fire must be returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבן גמליאל: he uses the פסוק for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל does not read the פסוק as a limit on which items stay up. For him it teaches that pieces of an offering that fell off the fire must be put back. So the פסוק does not go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pieces that jumped off the fire

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע learns from 'עֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה' that only things fit for the fire stay up. רבן גמליאל uses the same פסוק to teach that fallen pieces must be put back.

phrases.english: That [verse], to return dislodged pieces
is what it comes [to teach].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is used for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק limits which items stay on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבן גמליאל, the פסוק teaches putting fallen pieces back on the fire.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהושע learn to return pieces that jumped off the fire?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל learned the rule about returning פּוֹקְעִין from 'על מוקדה'. רבי יהושע already used those words for his main rule, so where does he learn it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהושע: from where does he learn that pieces that jumped off the fire must be put back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יהושע and asks where he gets the rule about putting back pieces that jumped off the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבן גמליאל learned this rule from 'עולה על מוקדה'. רבי יהושע used that same phrase for his main rule, which is that only things fit for the fire stay up. So that phrase is not free for him, and he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other תנא)
Pieces that popped or jumped off the fire
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And the other one —
phrases.notes: Here 'the other one' is רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: to return pieces that jumped off the fire, from where does he learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 used 'על מוקדה' for פוקעין according to רבן גמליאל. Now the גמרא asks for רבי יהושע's source for the same rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע used up 'על מוקדה', so he seems to have no source for returning פוקעין.

steps.title: רבי יהושע learns it from 'that the fire consumes'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע learns the rule about returning פוקעין from the words 'אשר תאכל האש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'that the fire consumes'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע has a different phrase: 'אשר תאכל האש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase speaks about what the fire has already been eating. It shows that something the fire has already started to burn goes back, even if it jumped off.

phrases.english: He learns it from 'that the fire consumes.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an alternate פסוק as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע has no source for returning פוקעין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from 'אשר תאכל האש'.

steps.title: What does רבן גמליאל do with 'that the fire consumes'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבן גמליאל learns from 'אשר תאכל האש', since he did not need it for פוקעין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבן גמליאל: what does he do with this phrase?
steps.whatsHappening: In one word, the גמרא sets up its next question. If רבן גמליאל learned פוקעין from 'על מוקדה', what is 'אשר תאכל האש' for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no words in the תורה are extra. Since רבן גמליאל got the פוקעין rule elsewhere, this phrase must teach him something else.

phrases.english: And the other one —
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבן גמליאל: what does he learn from 'אשר תאכל האש'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same question around onto רבן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבן גמליאל learns from 'אשר תאכל האש'.

steps.title: Burnt pieces of an עולה go back, but burnt pieces of קטורת do not
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל needs 'אשר תאכל האש' to teach that you return partly burnt pieces of an עולה but not of קטורת. A ברייתא of רבי חנינא בר מניומי supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that phrase to teach: you return partly burnt pieces of an עולה, but you do not return partly burnt pieces of קטורת. As רבי חנינא בר מניומי, son of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, taught: 'That the fire consumes the עולה on the מזבח' teaches that you return partly burnt pieces of an עולה, but you do not return partly burnt pieces of קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל uses the phrase for a limit: the rule of putting burnt pieces back applies to an עולה but not to קטורת. It brings a ברייתא that says exactly this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק says 'the fire consumes the עולה'. It names the עולה, so the rule of returning is limited to sacrifices like the עולה, and incense that fell off is not put back.

phrases.english: He needs that for:
partly burnt pieces of a burnt offering you return,
but you do not return partly burnt pieces of incense.
As Rabbi Ḥanina bar Minyumi taught,
son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ –
phrases.english: 'That the fire consumes the burnt offering on the altar' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3. Notice that the פסוק names the עולה. That is the key word.

phrases.english: partly burnt pieces of a burnt offering you return,
but you do not return partly burnt pieces of incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: לְעִכּוּלֵי עוֹלָה אַתָּה מַחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן גמליאל uses 'אשר תאכל האש' to exclude burnt pieces of קטורת from being returned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a practical rule: partly burnt incense that fell off the altar is not put back.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהושע learn the incense rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע used 'אשר תאכל האש' for פוקעין, so where does he learn that קטורת is not returned?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהושע: from where does he learn that burnt pieces of קטורת are not returned?
steps.whatsHappening: In one word, the גמרא sets up its next question. רבי יהושע used this phrase for פוקעין, so where does he get the incense rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase seems to be used up by one teaching. So the גמרא checks whether רבי יהושע is missing a source for the קטורת limit.

phrases.english: And the other one —
phrases.notes: Back to רבי יהושע. The question is: where does he learn that incense is not put back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether רבי יהושע has a source for the rule taught in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהושע's source for not returning partly burnt קטורת.

steps.title: The incense limit comes on its own from the word 'עולה'
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק that teaches returning burnt pieces names the עולה. So it already shows that only the עולה's pieces are returned, and not the קטורת's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't we already hear on our own from it that it is burnt pieces of an עולה that we return?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע does not need a separate source. One פסוק can teach both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע learns from 'אשר תאכל האש את העולה' that partly burnt pieces go back. Since the פסוק says 'העולה', it is automatically clear that this is only about the עולה and not about קטורת. So one phrase gives both the rule and its limit.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע learns from 'אשר תאכל האש את העולה' that partly burnt pieces go back. The word 'עולה' itself limits this to the עולה, so burnt incense is not returned.

phrases.english: Do you not hear on its own from it
that it is burnt pieces of a burnt offering that we return?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קטורת limit comes automatically from the word 'עולה' in the same פסוק.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבן גמליאל says anything fit for the מזבח stays up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words of רבן גמליאל: anything fit for the מזבח does not come down once it went up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: anything fit for the מזבח, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה to set up a new question about the word 'מזבח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל learns his wider rule from the word 'מזבח' in 'היא העולה על מוקדה על המזבח'. רבי יהושע learns his narrower rule, that only things fit for the fire stay up, from 'מוקדה'.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (short for the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Anything that is fit, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the משנה's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן גמליאל, anything fit for the מזבח stays once it has gone up.

steps.title: רבי יהושע also has the word 'מזבח' in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק also says 'מזבח', so why doesn't רבי יהושע agree with רבן גמליאל's wider rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יהושע too, isn't it written 'מזבח'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע. The word 'מזבח' is in the same פסוק, so what does he do with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מזבח' teaches that whatever is fit for the altar stays, then רבי יהושע should say this too. Otherwise he must have some other use for the word.

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yehoshua too,
isn't it written 'altar'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2: 'היא העולה על מוקדה על המזבח'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע using the word that רבן גמליאל relies on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'מזבח' is in his פסוק too, so it should teach him the wider rule.

steps.title: 'מזבח' teaches the reason: the altar makes things holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע uses 'מזבח' to explain why fit items stay up: the מזבח makes them holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word to teach: why did the תורה say that anything fit for the fire stays up? Because the מזבח makes it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע uses the word 'מזבח' to give the reason behind his rule, not to make the rule wider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, 'מוקדה' tells us what stays up: things fit for the fire. 'מזבח' tells us why they stay: the מזבח makes holy whatever touches it. So the word is used, but not to include more items.

keyTerms.meaning: The pyre / the burning fire on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים read the same פסוק. רבן גמליאל uses 'מזבח' to include anything fit for the altar. רבי יהושע limits the rule to things fit for the fire ('מוקדה') and uses 'מזבח' only for the reason: the מזבח makes them holy.

phrases.english: He needs that for:
what is the reason the Merciful One said
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'טעמא'. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: anything fit for the pyre stays up?
Because the altar makes it holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: מַאי (טַעְמָא) קָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word another use (it teaches the reason, not a wider rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מזבח' should give רבי יהושע the wider rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהושע, 'מזבח' gives the reason: the מזבח makes holy what is fit for the fire.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement holds. Each תנא reads the words of the פסוק in his own way.

steps.title: Where רבן גמליאל learns that the altar makes things holy
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל uses the 'מזבח' of the עולה פסוק for his wider rule. He learns that the מזבח makes things holy from a different פסוק that also says 'מזבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבן גמליאל), where does he learn it? Another 'מזבח' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבן גמליאל knows that the מזבח makes items holy, since he already used the word 'מזבח' for his own rule. It answers that a second פסוק also says 'מזבח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, רבי יהושע used 'מזבח' to teach that the מזבח makes things holy. רבן גמליאל needs that same word for his wide rule that anything fit for the מזבח stays up. So he takes the idea that the מזבח makes things holy from a different פסוק: 'כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש'.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other תנא in the argument
It is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: And the other one (Rabban Gamliel)?
Another 'altar' is written.
phrases.notes: שמות 29:37: 'כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 15: now that רבי יהושע's use of 'מזבח' is explained, the גמרא explains where רבן גמליאל gets the same idea.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבן גמליאל learns that the מזבח makes items holy.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From a second mention of 'מזבח' in שמות 29:37.

steps.title: Why רבי יהושע needs both altar verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע has both 'מזבח' פסוקים teaching the same thing. One covers an item that was once fit and then became disqualified. The other covers an item that was never fit at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יהושע)? One פסוק is for a case where the item had a time of being fit, and one is for a case where it never had a time of being fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע needs two פסוקים that both say the מזבח makes things holy. It answers that each one covers a different kind of disqualified item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, both mentions of 'מזבח' seem to teach the same rule, so one looks extra. The answer splits the cases. One פסוק covers an item that was fit for a while and then became disqualified, for example by becoming טמא. The other covers an item that was disqualified from the very start.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when the item was fit to be offered

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases here are about items that end up פסול. 'Had a time of being fit' means the item was fine for a while before it became פסול. It does not mean the item is fit now.

phrases.english: And the other one (Rabbi Yehoshua)?

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְהֵיכָא דְּהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר,
phrases.english: One is for where it had a time of fitness,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְהֵיכָא דְּלֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: and one is for where it did not have a time of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – חַד לְהֵיכָא דְּהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 16 showed a second 'מזבח' פסוק. That makes רבי יהושע look like he has an extra פסוק, and this step explains why he needs it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע seems to have two פסוקים teaching the same rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק covers a different kind of disqualified item.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of the two 'מזבח' פסוקים is extra for רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק covers items that were once fit, and the other covers items that were never fit.

steps.title: Why רבן גמליאל does not need a separate verse for each case
steps.stepSummary: For רבן גמליאל, once the תורה included disqualified items at all, it makes no difference whether they were ever fit. One פסוק is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבן גמליאל)? Since they are disqualified items and the Merciful One included them anyway, it makes no difference whether the item had a time of fitness or did not have a time of fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבן גמליאל is fine with only one פסוק for disqualified items. His view is that once the תורה included פסול items, every kind of פסול item is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע needed two פסוקים to cover both kinds of פסול items. רבן גמליאל says there is no need to split them. The תורה already decided that even פסול items stay on the מזבח, so whether the item was once fit makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the תורה) included them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע: one 'מזבח' teaches that the מזבח makes things holy for items that were once fit, and the other for items never fit. רבן גמליאל: one 'מזבח' for his wide rule, one for the מזבח making things holy, and all פסול items are treated the same.

phrases.english: And the other one (Rabban Gamliel)?
Since they are disqualified items
and the Merciful One included them,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
phrases.english: it is no different if it had a time of fitness

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לֹא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: and no different if it did not have a time of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – כֵּיוָן דִּפְסוּלִין נִינְהוּ וְרַבִּינְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the opposite question: why רבן גמליאל does not need the split that רבי יהושע made in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל seems to be missing a פסוק for items that were never fit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning: once פסול items are included, all of them are included.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each kind of פסול item would need its own פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the תורה includes פסול items, it makes no difference whether they were ever fit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only things that come for their own sake stay on the altar
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה, a ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's source. From the word 'עולה' he learns that only items brought for their own sake stay up. נסכים, which come because of the animal offering, are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the זבח is fit, and so on. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, 'עולה': just as an עולה comes for its own sake, so too anything that comes for its own sake. This leaves out נסכים, which come because of a זבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the start of רבי שמעון's opinion. It then brings a ברייתא that shows where רבי שמעון learns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון compares other items to the עולה. Only things that are brought on their own, as the עולה is, stay on the מזבח. נסכים only come along with an animal offering, so they do not stay up even if they already went up.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake, on its own account
Wine poured on the מזבח that comes with an offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's surprising result: the זבח stays up even when it is פסול, but the נסכים come down even when they are fit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַזֶּבַח כָּשֵׁר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: The offering is fit, etc.
It was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
'Burnt offering': just as a burnt offering comes for its own sake,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

phrases.english: so too all things that come for their own sake;
excluded are libations, which come because of an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל, the גמרא moves on to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only items that come for their own sake, as the עולה does, stay on the מזבח. נסכים, which come because of a זבח, come down.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the מזבח only makes fit items holy, learned from 'כבשים'
steps.stepSummary: 'כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש' could sound like it covers everything. רבי יוסי הגלילי limits it to fit items by comparing them to the כבשים in the next פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: since it says 'Whatever touches the מזבח shall be holy,' I would understand both fit and unfit items. So the פסוק says 'lambs': just as lambs are fit, so too only what is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. In it, רבי יוסי הגלילי shows that the מזבח only makes holy those items that are fit for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, 'כל הנוגע' sounds like the מזבח makes anything at all holy. The next פסוק talks about כבשים, which are proper offerings. That shows the rule is only about items fit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From that which is stated: 'Whatever touches the altar shall be sacred,'
phrases.notes: שמות 29:37

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי בֵּין רָאוּי וּבֵין שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי;
phrases.english: I would understand both what is fit and what is unfit;
therefore the verse states: 'lambs,'
phrases.notes: שמות 29:38, the very next פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: מָה כְּבָשִׂים רְאוּיִין, אַף כֹּל רָאוּי.
phrases.english: just as lambs are fit, so too everything that is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that limits the 'כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש' פסוק mentioned in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח only makes items holy if they are fit for it, as the כבשים are.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the same limit, learned from 'burnt offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא agrees that only fit items are made holy. He learns it from the word 'עולה' instead of 'כבשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'עולה': just as an עולה is fit, so too only what is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא reaches the same result as רבי יוסי הגלילי from a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that the מזבח only makes fit items holy. The only difference is the source: רבי יוסי הגלילי compares to the כבשים, and רבי עקיבא compares to the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too: a comparison used to learn one thing from another

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי (from 'כבשים') and רבי עקיבא (from 'עולה') agree: the מזבח only makes holy what is fit for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Burnt offering': just as a burnt offering is fit,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

phrases.english: so too everything that is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: עֹלָה – מָה עוֹלָה רְאוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same rule taught in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח only makes items holy if they are fit for it, as the עולה is.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between ר׳ יוסי הגלילי (learning from 'כבשים') and ר׳ עקיבא (learning from 'עולה').
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two different sources lead to any different result. This sets up the next step, where רב אדא בר אהבה answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that only fit items are made holy by the מזבח. They just learn it from different words in the פסוק. The גמרא wants to know if the choice of word changes the הלכה in any case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא from the last two steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two sources given in steps 20-21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where learning from 'עולה' gives a different result than learning from 'כבשים'.

steps.title: They differ about a disqualified bird burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה: a disqualified עולת העוף is the difference. ר׳ עקיבא, who learns from 'עולה', includes it. ר׳ יוסי הגלילי, who learns from 'כבשים', does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: A disqualified bird burnt offering is the difference between them. One master learns it from 'עולה', and the other master learns it from 'כבשים'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives the case where the two sources lead to different results: a bird עולה that became disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird is still an עולה, so ר׳ עקיבא's word 'עולה' covers it, and it stays on the מזבח. A bird is not like a lamb, so ר׳ יוסי הגלילי's word 'כבשים' does not cover it, and it must come down.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering of a bird

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
A disqualified bird burnt offering is the difference between them;
one master learns it from 'burnt offering',
phrases.notes: This is ר׳ עקיבא. A bird is also an עולה, so it is included.

phrases.english: and the other master learns it from 'lambs'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה עוֹלַת הָעוֹף פְּסוּלָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A disqualified bird עולה stays up according to ר׳ עקיבא ('עולה') but not according to ר׳ יוסי הגלילי ('כבשים').
steps.whatToRemember: ר׳ עקיבא learns from 'עולה' and includes a disqualified bird. ר׳ יוסי הגלילי learns from 'כבשים' and leaves the bird out.

steps.title: But the word 'עולה' is also written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ר׳ יוסי הגלילי: the פסוק also says 'עולה', so why doesn't he learn from it and include birds?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns it from 'כבשים', isn't 'עולה' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ר׳ יוסי הגלילי. The word 'עולה' is right there in the פסוק, so why doesn't he use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'עולה' is written, it looks like it should include birds, the way it does for ר׳ עקיבא. The גמרא wants to know what ר׳ יוסי הגלילי does with that word.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who...

phrases.english: And according to the one who learns it from 'lambs' —
isn't 'burnt offering' written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּמַיְיתֵי לַהּ מִכְּבָשִׂים הָכְתִיב עֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ר׳ יוסי הגלילי's side of the dispute set out in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: ר׳ יוסי הגלילי's choice to learn from 'כבשים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'עולה' is also in the פסוק and seems to include birds. Why does he ignore it?

steps.title: 'עולה' teaches that live animals are not included
steps.stepSummary: For ר׳ יוסי הגלילי, 'עולה' is needed for something else. Without it, one might think even a live animal that went up stays up. 'עולה' limits the rule to an offering ready for the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'כבשים' were written and 'עולה' were not written, I would have said that even live animals are included. So the תורה wrote 'עולה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ר׳ יוסי הגלילי uses the word 'עולה' for a different lesson. It teaches that a live animal is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כבשים' alone could mean lambs in any state, even alive. 'עולה' shows the rule is about an offering that is going up to be burned. So for ר׳ יוסי הגלילי the word is already used up and cannot include birds.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: If 'lambs' were written and 'burnt offering' were not written,
I would have said even while alive;
phrases.notes: He means a disqualified animal that went up on the מזבח alive. 'עולה' shows that it does not stay there.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote 'burnt offering'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתִיב כְּבָשִׂים וְלָא כְּתִיב עֹלָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲפִילּוּ מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word is given a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'כבשים', even a live disqualified animal would stay on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עולה' leaves out live animals, so ר׳ יוסי הגלילי cannot use it to include birds.

steps.title: But the word 'כבשים' is also written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ר׳ עקיבא: the פסוק also says 'כבשים', so why doesn't he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns it from 'עולה', isn't 'כבשים' written?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the same kind of question on ר׳ עקיבא. What does he do with the word 'כבשים'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'כבשים' is written, it seems to limit the rule to animals like lambs. The גמרא asks what lesson ר׳ עקיבא takes from that word.

phrases.english: And according to the one who learns it from 'burnt offering',
isn't 'lambs' written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּמַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ מֵעֹלָה הָא כְּתִיב כְּבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a matching challenge on the other side of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: ר׳ עקיבא's choice to learn from 'עולה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'כבשים' is also in the פסוק. What does he learn from it?

steps.title: 'כבשים' teaches that a מנחה is not included
steps.stepSummary: For ר׳ עקיבא, without 'כבשים' one might think even a מנחה is included. 'כבשים' limits the rule to animal and bird offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'עולה' were written and 'כבשים' were not written, I would have said that even a מנחה is included. So the תורה wrote 'כבשים'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ר׳ עקיבא uses 'כבשים' to leave out a מנחה (flour offering).
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עולה' alone could cover anything that goes up on the מזבח, even flour. 'כבשים' shows the rule is only for animal offerings, and the word 'עולה' adds birds. So each תנא uses both words, but each word teaches a different limit.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use both words. ר׳ יוסי הגלילי: 'כבשים' gives the main rule, and 'עולה' leaves out live animals. ר׳ עקיבא: 'עולה' gives the main rule and includes birds, and 'כבשים' leaves out a מנחה.

phrases.english: If 'burnt offering' were written and 'lambs' were not written,
I would have said even a meal offering;
so the Merciful One wrote 'lambs'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתִיב עֹלָה וְלָא כְּתִיב כְּבָשִׂים הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word is given a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'עולה', even a disqualified מנחה would stay on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כבשים' leaves out a מנחה. Only animal and bird offerings stay up.

steps.title: How do these תנאים differ from the תנאים of our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the תנאים of the ברייתא and the תנאים of our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between these תנאים and the תנאים of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the ברייתא's תנאים (ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא) with the תנאים in our משנה. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה talks in general terms about what is fit for the מזבח or for the fire. The ברייתא limits the rule to animal and bird offerings. The גמרא looks for a case where these two approaches give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה period

phrases.english: What is there between these תנאים
phrases.notes: 'These תנאים' are ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and these תנאים of our משנה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא's sources, the גמרא compares the ברייתא to our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the ברייתא's תנאים and the משנה's תנאים give different rulings.

steps.title: They differ about קמצים that became holy in a כלי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: disqualified קמצים that were made holy in a כלי שרת are the difference. By our משנה they do not come down. By the ברייתא they do come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: קמצים that became holy in a כלי are the difference between them. According to our תנאים, they do not come down. According to the תנאים of the ברייתא, they do come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the difference shows up with a disqualified קומץ, the handful of flour taken from a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's rule covers anything fit for the מזבח, and a קומץ is fit, so it stays up. The ברייתא's תנאים learn from 'כבשים' and 'עולה' that a flour offering is left out, so the קומץ comes down.

keyTerms.meaning: Handfuls of flour taken from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
That became holy in a כלי שרת (service vessel)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two similar words. 'מתניתין' (step 28) means our משנה, but 'מתניתא' here means the ברייתא of ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא. 'Our תנאים' are the ones in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברייתא's reading of 'כבשים' and 'עולה' leaves out every flour offering. Our משנה's general rule does not leave them out.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
handfuls that were sanctified in a vessel are the difference between them —
phrases.notes: He means a קומץ that became holy in the כלי and was then disqualified, and then went up on the מזבח.

phrases.english: according to our תנאים, they shall not come down,
according to the תנאים of the ברייתא, they shall come down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא קְמָצִים שֶׁקָּדְשׁוּ בִּכְלִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Disqualified קמצים stay up according to our משנה but come down according to the ברייתא, which leaves out flour offerings.

steps.title: By all the משנה's opinions, a meal offering that comes by itself does not come down
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a מנחה brought on its own does not come down from the מזבח according to all the תנאים of our משנה. He then opens a second clause about ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: A meal offering that comes by itself does not come down, according to everyone. According to ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא...
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש starts a summary of who holds what. His first point is that a מנחה brought on its own stays on the מזבח according to all the תנאים of our משנה. His second point, about ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא, is only just beginning here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the תנאים of our משנה agree about a מנחה brought on its own, not alongside an animal offering. It is fit for the fire and for the מזבח, and it comes for its own sake, so it does not come down once it has gone up. The second half of the statement switches to the ברייתא's תנאים, ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא, who left out a מנחה in step 27. Their ruling continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made of flour
That comes by itself, not alongside an animal offering
According to everyone, meaning all the opinions
It does not come down from the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished. The part that starts 'according to ר׳ יוסי הגלילי and ר׳ עקיבא' gets its ruling on the next amud, so don't read 'it does not come down' as their ruling too.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A meal offering that comes by itself,
according to everyone, it does not come down;
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' means all the תנאים of our משנה. The ברייתא's תנאים are handled separately in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: according to the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and Rabbi Akiva,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא named one practical difference between the two groups of תנאים, ריש לקיש gives a broader summary of how the views apply, case by case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה brought on its own never comes down from the מזבח once it has gone up, according to all the תנאים of our משנה.
